body.statement: On the known exact-uniform class \(\mathcal M_H\), for \(n^{-1}\le\epsilon_n\le1\), the displayed unique joint-release mechanism admits a deterministic finite-grid choice of \((h,\ell)\), depending only on public parameters and using a fixed tie-break, for which \(T_{\mathrm{priv}}(h,\ell)\) is \(\epsilon_n\)-differentially private under replacement adjacency and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_H}\mathbb E_P|T_{\mathrm{priv}}(h,\ell)-\tau_P(x_0)|\le C\max\{b_n,\rho_n^{\mathrm{priv}}\}\). Before optimization its risk is bounded by \(C\{h^\gamma+\ell^q+(nh^d)^{-1/2}+(n^2h^d\ell^d)^{-1/2}+(n^2\epsilon_nh^d\ell^d)^{-1}\}\). No conclusion is asserted for an unknown bounded design density or for \(\epsilon_n<n^{-1}\).
body.justification: A total one-shot release is the constructive half of the incremental privacy frontier.
body.gap: Niu et al. prove privacy for modular meta-learners but no Hölder minimax utility bound; Chaudhuri et al. treat generic U-statistics rather than localized causal moments.
body.consumer: It gives private heterogeneous-effect learners a sharp benchmark in privacy-leading regimes and a fully auditable sensitivity ledger.
